title: Inverse image along an isomorphism of schemes on the pro-etale site
statement:
Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with small pro-etale sites $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $g^{-1}$, $g_*$ and the structure maps $c^g_A:g^{-1}A_Y\to A_X$ be the inverse image, direct image and structure maps of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Then:

1. The functor $\Phi_g:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $(U\xrightarrow{u}X)\mapsto(U\xrightarrow{g\circ u}Y)$, is an equivalence of categories, with quasi-inverse $(V\xrightarrow{v}Y)\mapsto(V\xrightarrow{g^{-1}\circ v}X)$; both functors send coverings to coverings. For every sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ there is an isomorphism $(g^{-1}\mathcal F)(U\xrightarrow{u}X)\cong\mathcal F(U\xrightarrow{g\circ u}Y)$, natural in $\mathcal F$ and in $U$.
2. $g^{-1}$ is an equivalence of categories from sheaves on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (of sets, abelian groups, rings, or modules over a constant sheaf of rings), with quasi-inverse $g_*$. In particular $g^{-1}$ is exact and commutes with all small limits and colimits; for every inverse system $(\mathcal F_n)_{n\geq1}$ of sheaves on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ the canonical map $g^{-1}\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n\to\varprojlim_ng^{-1}\mathcal F_n$ [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], induced by the inverse images of the projections, is an isomorphism.
3. For every commutative ring $A$ the structure map $c^g_A:g^{-1}A_Y\to A_X$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings, and for every ring homomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$, with $\varphi_Y:A_Y\to B_Y$ and $\varphi_X:A_X\to B_X$ the induced maps of constant sheaves, $\varphi_X\circ c^g_A=c^g_B\circ g^{-1}(\varphi_Y)$.

source.place: Stacks Project, Tag 09A5 (Section 'Functoriality of the pro-etale site'); Sites, Tag 06UM (Section sites-section-pullback) and Tag 0H7J (Example sites-example-constant-sheaf: Mor(E_C, F) = Mor(E, Gamma(C, F))). The specialization to an isomorphism g is not stated there; the source of this node is the construction of def-weil-constant-weil-structure and the point-transport construction of def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport, item 2, which uses part 1 for g_s

proof.text: Write h for the inverse of g. The diagonal of g is an isomorphism with inverse pr_1: g pr_1=g pr_2 implies pr_1=pr_2 after composing with h, so (pr_1,pr_2)=Delta_g pr_1. The same holds for h. An isomorphism and its diagonal induce isomorphisms on local rings, whose tensor functors identify with the identity under those ring isomorphisms: for a local-ring isomorphism alpha:R→S the maps N tensor_R S→N and N→N tensor_R S send x tensor s to alpha^{-1}(s)x and x to x tensor 1, respectively. They are inverse by the tensor relations and natural in N, hence preserve injections. The flat-module criterion [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and stalkwise definition [def-weil-flat-morphism] show that the isomorphisms are flat. Thus g and its inverse h are weakly etale [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism]. By weakly etale composition, postcomposition defines functors Phi_g and Phi_h; their composites are identities on objects and arrows, up to the chosen small-skeleton identifications. The underlying morphisms in a covering family do not change, so the fpqc and weakly etale covering conditions are unchanged. Write U_Y=(U,g u). In the comma category I_U of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], take D_U=(U_Y,theta_U), where theta_U=(u,id_U):U→X×_Y U_Y. For any (V,phi), the map a=pr_2 phi:U_Y→V is the unique arrow D_U→(V,phi): indeed u_g(a) theta_U=phi by the two fibre-product projections, and that equation forces a=pr_2 phi. Therefore D_U is initial in I_U and terminal in I_U^op. Explicitly the colimit is F(U_Y): its cocone from F(V) is restriction along a, its inverse is the coprojection indexed by D_U, and the cocone equations and the unique arrows from D_U show both composites are identities. For b:U'→U, the formula a=pr_2 phi gives restriction along b_Y:U'_Y→U_Y; for a sheaf morphism it gives its component at U_Y. Hence the identification is natural in U and F. The presheaf U↦F(U_Y) is already a sheaf: a covering and its overlap objects become exactly the corresponding covering and overlaps over Y, so its matching-family equalizer is the sheaf equalizer for F. Its sheafification is itself by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], proving the section formula.

source.place: Tag 09A5, proetale-section-morphism; Sites Tag 00VC, sites-section-functoriality-PSh, equation sites-equation-colim-category (053L), and Lemma 00WX, sites-lemma-adjoint-sheaves; More on Morphisms Tags 094P, 094T and 094U; Algebra Tag 00HB, algebra-definition-flat

proof.text: Define T(F)(U)=F(U_Y) and S(G)(V)=G(V_X), where V_X=(V,h v) and h is the inverse scheme isomorphism. Step 1 shows these are sheaves and g^{-1}≅T. For each U and V, (U_Y)_X=U and (V_X)_Y=V; the identities on their sections are natural unit and counit isomorphisms ST≅id and TS≅id (with the canonical representative isomorphisms on small skeletons). Moreover X×_Y V≅V_X over X, with forward map pr_2 and inverse (h v,id_V); restriction along this isomorphism identifies the recorded g_*G(V)=G(X×_Y V) with S(G)(V), naturally in V and G. The adjunction in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], equivalently [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] for sets and abelian groups, is thus the adjunction of these mutually inverse functors. For abelian-group sheaves, T and S take addition, zero and negation at U or V to the very same operations at U_Y or V_X. For ring sheaves they also take multiplication and unit to those operations there. The section isomorphism from the comma colimit respects each operation, by its construction from restriction homomorphisms; hence these identifications are with the abelian and ring inverse images defined in the cited definition, and the unit and counit are homomorphisms. This establishes the equivalences for sets, abelian groups and rings. Apply [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits] to obtain preservation of all existing small limits and colimits. In the abelian-group category, kernels and cokernels are the corresponding finite limits and colimits, so the additive equivalence is exact; for sets and rings the equivalence preserves finite limits and finite colimits as well.

Let P_Y and P_X be the constant ring presheaves with value A, and let T,S denote the inverse transports of Step 2, also on presheaves. Then T(P_Y)=P_X. The sheaf T(A_Y), with its map P_X→T(A_Y), is a sheafification of P_X: a presheaf map P_X→H to an X-sheaf corresponds by S to P_Y→S(H), extends uniquely to A_Y→S(H) by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and applying T gives its unique extension T(A_Y)→H. Thus uniqueness of sheafification gives an isomorphism beta_A:T(A_Y)→A_X taking the image of every constant a to the image of the same a. This proves isomorphy without assuming that all sections of a constant sheaf are constant. Under Step 1 the candidate beta_A∘(g^{-1}A_Y≅T(A_Y)) has adjoint A_Y→g_*A_X sending each a∈P_Y(V) to its constant section over X×_Y V: the adjunction unit is the comma-colimit coprojection at (V,id), and the colimit identification is restriction along pr_2:(X×_Y V)_Y→V. Uniqueness of the extension from P_Y says this adjoint is exactly rho^g_A in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Consequently the candidate is c^g_A, hence c^g_A is an isomorphism. For a ring homomorphism phi:A→B, identify the source of both proposed composites with T(A_Y), itself the sheafification of P_X. On the constant generator a, both composites give the constant section phi(a); uniqueness of extension from P_X makes the two sheaf maps equal. This is the required naturality equation.

source.place: Tag 0H7J, sites-example-constant-sheaf; Proposition 00WH, sites-proposition-sheafification-adjoint; Lemma 00VE, sites-lemma-adjoints-u, and Lemma 00WX, sites-lemma-adjoint-sheaves; Pro-etale Tag 09A5, proetale-section-morphism

proof.text: Use beta_A:T(A_Y)≅A_X from Step 3. For an A_Y-module sheaf F, define the action on T(F)(U)=F(U_Y) by b⋅x=beta_{A,U}^{-1}(b)x for b∈A_X(U). The identities (b+b')x=bx+b'x, b(x+x')=bx+bx', (bb')x=b(b'x) and 1x=x follow from the A_Y(U_Y)-module identities and the fact that beta_A is a ring homomorphism. Restrictions are semilinear because beta_A commutes with restrictions; a transported module morphism is linear by the same formula. This is the transported inverse image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] after its scalar extension: at U the defining tensor presheaf maps to T(F)(U) by x⊗b↦beta_{A,U}^{-1}(b)x, with inverse x↦x⊗1; the tensor relations make these inverse and compatible with restrictions. By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and sheafification's universal property this identifies the tensor-defined module pullback with T(F). On an A_X-module sheaf G, define S(G)(V)=G(V_X) with the A_Y(V)-action obtained by applying S to beta_A:A_Y≅S(A_X). The isomorphism X×_Y V≅V_X of Step 2 identifies this action with the action through rho^g_{A,V} defining the actual module direct image: both ring maps agree on constant sections, hence agree by sheafification uniqueness as maps A_Y→g_*A_X. The underlying identities ST(F)≅F and TS(G)≅G respect actions, since their scalar maps are beta_A and its inverse. They therefore give inverse module equivalences with the specified g_*. These functors preserve addition on morphisms, and [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits] gives all limits and colimits, in particular kernels and cokernels in the abelian categories of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; hence the module inverse image is exact.

proof.text: Apply preservation of limits from Steps 2 and 4 to the inverse-system diagram (F_n) in the sheaf category. For modules, abelian groups and rings, [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] supplies the sectionwise compatible-family limit and its coordinate projections. For sets the same compatible-family presheaf is a sheaf: glue a matching family coordinate by coordinate using each F_n; the transition equations hold for the glued sections because they hold after restriction to the covering and F_n is separated. A cone maps uniquely to this sheaf by the tuple of its coordinate maps, so it is the limit also in sets. The image of the original limit cone is a limit cone by [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits]. Its comparison with the chosen limit of (g^{-1}F_n)_n is therefore invertible: the two maps furnished by the limit universal properties have identity composites since their composites with every projection are identities. By construction its composites with the projections are the inverse images of the original coordinate projections. Thus it is exactly the canonical comparison map specified in the statement.

The module publicly imports the original module, retaining every old site equivalence, comma-normalized comparison, canonical constant-ring comparison/naturality and module-equivalence declaration.
